jobs.description:
About Us

Stimulus Technologies is a leader in technology services, dedicated to bridging the digital divide in underserved communities. With operations across California, Missouri, Nevada, New Mexico, and Oregon, we deliver high-speed, reliable connectivity that transforms lives and businesses. We also offer IT, VoIP, and CyberSecurity services to a range of clients.

Position Overview

Own the project. Navigate the complexity. Deliver on the promise.

As a Project Manager at Stimulus Technologies, you lead grant-funded fiber deployment projects from design kickoff through construction and final network turnover, where execution isn’t just about timelines, but strict compliance, funding milestones, and public accountability. You are the single point of ownership for delivering projects that meet aggressive build schedules while satisfying state and federal grant requirements.

This is a high-ownership role where you’ll manage competing priorities across engineering partners, contractors, internal teams, and clients, while ensuring every decision aligns with budget, schedule, and reimbursement eligibility. You’ll proactively manage risk, enforce accountability, and keep projects moving in an environment where delays and missteps have real financial consequences. If you thrive in complex, high-stakes projects and want to lead work that directly impacts communities, this is your opportunity to take ownership and deliver at scale.

Essential Functions

Project Planning and Schedule Management

Develop and maintain the master project schedule encompassing design, permitting, construction, drop installation, testing, and network turnover milestones.
Coordinate schedule dependencies across the engineering firm (design and permitting), construction contractors (mainline build), and in-house crews (drop installation) to ensure alignment and prevent downstream delays.
Establish project milestones and critical path items; proactively identify schedule risks and develop mitigation plans.
Track and enforce compliance with grant-mandated buildout timelines, reporting deadlines, and program-specific milestone requirements.
Manage project scope and change control processes; evaluate and document the cost, schedule, and scope impact of all change requests before approval.
Facilitate project kickoff meetings and establish roles, responsibilities, and communication cadences with all internal and external stakeholders.

SOW, Contract, and Budget Management

Monitor the engineering firm’s performance against their SOW, deliverable schedules, and contract terms; document deviations and coordinate corrective actions with the Construction Manager and Director of Project Management.
Monitor construction contractor performance against contract terms, pay application accuracy, and change order justifications in coordination with the Construction Manager.
Develop and manage project budgets; track actual costs against forecasts and report variances to the Director of Project Management.
Review and approve invoices from the engineering firm, construction contractors, and permitting agencies for accuracy and contract alignment before processing.
Ensure all project expenditures are properly documented and categorized for grant reimbursement and compliance reporting.
Maintain organized contract files including SOWs, amendments, change orders, and correspondence for each project.

Stakeholder and Client Management

Serve as the primary point of contact for the client on project status, deliverables, and issue resolution.
Prepare and deliver regular project status reports to the client, Director of Project Management, and internal leadership including schedule performance, budget status, risks, and upcoming milestones.
Facilitate regular project status meetings with the client, engineering firm, construction contractors, and internal teams.
Manage client expectations and proactively communicate schedule or scope changes with proposed solutions.
Coordinate with the client on subscriber enrollment, service activation timelines, and drop installation priorities.

Cross-Functional Coordination

Coordinate with the Construction Manager on construction progress, contractor issues, and field resource needs.
Coordinate with the Permitting Manager on permit submittal schedules, approval status, and any permitting constraints affecting the construction schedule.
Coordinate with the Drop Installation Crew Manager on drop scheduling, production rates, and compliance with mandated installation timelines.
Work with the engineering firm to track design and permitting deliverable progress and ensure deliverables feed into the construction schedule on time.
Coordinate the construction-to-operations turnover process, ensuring all documentation, testing, and acceptance criteria are met before network handoff.
Identify resource conflicts or bottlenecks across projects and work with the Director of Project Management to prioritize and resolve.

Grant Compliance and Reporting

Ensure all project activities and documentation comply with state and federal grant program requirements.
Prepare and submit required grant reports, progress updates, and milestone certifications on schedule.
Maintain auditable project records including schedules, budgets, invoices, change orders, and deliverable logs for grant compliance purposes.
Track grant reimbursement submissions and coordinate with finance on draw schedules and funding status.
Stay current on grant program requirements and proactively communicate any compliance risks to the Director of Project Management.

Education and Experience

Required

High school diploma or GED; bachelor’s degree in project management, construction management, engineering, business, or related field preferred.
Minimum 5 years of project management experience in telecom, broadband, fiber optic, or utility construction.
Demonstrated experience managing project budgets, schedules, and contractor/vendor relationships.
Strong understanding of OSP fiber optic construction phases including design, permitting, mainline build, and drop installation.
Experience with SOW and contract compliance management for third-party engineering or construction firms.
Proficiency with project management tools (e.g., Microsoft Project, Smartsheet, or equivalent) and Microsoft Office Suite.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills for client-facing reporting and stakeholder management.
Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple concurrent projects and competing priorities.
Valid driver’s license with the ability to travel to project sites as needed.

Preferred

PMP certification or equivalent project management credential.
Experience with government-funded or grant-funded broadband deployment programs (BEAD, RDOF, ReConnect, CAF, or similar).
Familiarity with FTTH/FTTP deployment at scale.
Background in OSP engineering or construction management.
Experience with grant compliance reporting and reimbursement processes.

Alignment with Core Values

At Stimulus Technologies, our core values define how we work. The ideal candidate will demonstrate:

Driven to Grow – Continuously seeks to develop professionally, stays current with industry practices, and pushes to improve processes and outcomes.
See a Need – Fill a Need – Proactively identifies gaps, obstacles, or opportunities and takes action without waiting to be asked.
Elevate Others – Mentors teammates, shares knowledge freely, and actively contributes to a positive and collaborative work environment.
Extreme Ownership – Takes full accountability for results, decisions, and mistakes; does not deflect blame or make excuses.
Celebrate Success – Recognizes contributions of team members, acknowledges milestones, and fosters a culture where wins are shared.

Stimulus Technologies is an equal opportunity employer. This job description is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities, or qualifications associated with the position. Management reserves the right to amend and change responsibilities to meet business and organizational needs as necessary.

PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES
1. Development Operations & Database Architecture ● Campaign & CRM Architecture: Design and build the technical setup for annual appeals, special events, and fundraising campaigns in DonorPerfect (or primary CRM)—configuring appeal codes, campaign fields, online donation forms, and auto-acknowledgment workflows. ● Gift Processing & Acknowledgments: Oversee end-to-end gift processing for all gifts from data entry to acknowledgement to ensure compliance with tax guidelines and best practices in philanthropy. ● Data Hygiene & Integrity: Enforce data entry standards, conduct regular database audits, manage duplicate records, and ensure clean, segmented donor lists for advancement and communications efforts. ● Reconciliation & Reporting: Pull or support staff in developing regular campaign progress reports and analytics to support development strategy and financial batch reports to reconcile revenue monthly with accounting records.

2. Finance Administration ● Coding & Expense Tracking: Review, code, and route incoming invoices, credit card expenses, and vendor bills to ensure proper allocation across chart of accounts and department budgets. ● Outsourced Accounting Liaison: Serve as the internal operational link to FONA’s external accounting firm (YPTC)—submitting weekly revenue batches, accounts payable documentation, and payroll inputs.

new_jobs.description:
POSITION OVERVIEW Friends of the National Arboretum seeks a systems-minded, detail-oriented Senior Manager of Development and Business Operations to serve as the engine behind our fundraising systems, technology infrastructure, and internal operations. Rather than focusing on copy, creative, or solicitations, this role owns the technical and administrative architecture that makes fundraising and daily operations possible. From configuring campaign logic and managing data flows across systems (CRM, Eventbrite, website, email) to entering gifts, maintaining ledger hygiene, and managing basic office logistics, this position ensures FONA’s back-office operations run accurately, securely, and seamlessly.

ABOUT US Friends of the National Arboretum (FONA) is a nonprofit membership organization working to preserve and enhance the U.S. National Arboretum (USNA) in Washington D.C. and bring this remarkable resource to life as an important part of the city and region. Founded in 1982, FONA has served as the Arboretum’s primary nonprofit partner for over 40 years and funds critical operations, youth education programs, visitor services, and infrastructure improvements.

ABOUT YOU The ideal candidate will have experience with the following: ● Experience: 3–5 years of hands-on experience in nonprofit development operations, database administration, or business/financial operations. ● Technical Proficiency: Demonstrated experience configuring and managing a nonprofit CRM (FONA uses DonorPerfect) and setting up online gift processing workflows. ● Financial Literacy: Familiarity with nonprofit chart-of-accounts structures, gift coding, restricted fund tracking, and monthly reconciliation processes. ● Systems Mindset: Experience setting up or managing platform integrations (e.g., Zapier, CRM-to-Eventbrite syncs, email marketing tools). ● Attention to Detail: Meticulous organizational skills with a strong track record of data accuracy and process documentation.

PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES
1. Development Operations & Database Architecture ● Campaign & CRM Architecture: Design and build the technical setup for annual appeals, special events, and fundraising campaigns in DonorPerfect (or primary CRM)—configuring appeal codes, campaign fields, online donation forms, and auto-acknowledgment workflows. ● Gift Processing & Acknowledgments: Oversee end-to-end gift processing for all gifts from data entry to acknowledgement to ensure compliance with tax guidelines and best practices in philanthropy. ● Data Hygiene & Integrity: Enforce data entry standards, conduct regular database audits, manage duplicate records, and ensure clean, segmented donor lists for advancement and communications efforts. ● Reconciliation & Reporting: Pull or support staff in developing regular campaign progress reports and analytics to support development strategy and financial batch reports to reconcile revenue monthly with accounting records.

2. Finance Administration ● Coding & Expense Tracking: Review, code, and route incoming invoices, credit card expenses, and vendor bills to ensure proper allocation across chart of accounts and department budgets. ● Outsourced Accounting Liaison: Serve as the internal operational link to FONA’s external accounting firm (YPTC)—submitting weekly revenue batches, accounts payable documentation, and payroll inputs.

3. Systems Integration & Technology Infrastructure ● Cross-Platform Workflows: Lead technical integrations and data syncs between core platforms, including the CRM, website, Eventbrite, email marketing tools, and payment gateways. ● System Administration: Manage user access, subscription renewals, security settings, and basic technical troubleshooting across FONA’s core operational software stack.

4. Daily Operations & Office Management ● Office & Inventory Logistics: Manage physical supplies, organizational inventory, mail distribution, and day-to-day facilities needs at Arbor House (FONA offices) ● Vendor & Service Management: Oversee routine operational vendor relationships (office equipment, software subscriptions, mail services). ● Administrative Support: Support general organizational workflow tracking and assist leadership with administrative compliance filings as needed.

WORK SCHEDULE The work schedule is generally Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 5 PM, though schedules may shift to support events as needed. Office work at FONA is hybrid, to allow for on-site support, and staff flexibility. Work location will be a mix of both in-office (on the grounds of the U.S. National Arboretum) and remote as schedule allows. Salary is subject to FICA and income taxes. Excellent benefits package includes full health, dental and vision care coverage, a matching 401k retirement plan, paid federal holidays, generous accrued paid time off, and travel/cell phone/internet reimbursement.

COMPENSATION: $75,000 - $90,000, dependent on experience Expected start date: October/November 2026

TO APPLY Please send a cover letter and resume, with subject line “Senior Manager [Your Name]” to jobs@fona.org. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis after September 24.

To see the full position description, please visit https://www.fona.org/jobs-volunteering/

Our team is composed of highly skilled and knowledgeable professionals who excel across various disciplines. leads complex, multidisciplinary design and delivery efforts for advanced technology facilities, with a focus on cleanroom environments, fab support systems, and high-tech industrial infrastructure. This role manages scope, schedule, budget, quality, and risk across all phases of delivery, from early planning and basis of design through construction administration. The Senior Project Manager works closely with clients, discipline leads, subconsultants, and internal project teams to coordinate technical decisions, review design packages, resolve field issues, and maintain project momentum. The role also drives change management, best practices, and proactive communication to support predictable, high-quality project outcomes in fast-moving, highly regulated environments.

AI and Innovation

At SSOE, we don’t just talk about the future, we build it. As a leader in industry AI adoption, we empower our team to work smarter by providing responsible access to the industry leading AI Large Language Models, vibe-coding platforms, and securely integrating advanced tools into every role. From day one, you’ll receive the training and support needed to leverage AI as a core tool for enhancing productivity, sparking creativity, and streamlining complex workflows.

Responsibilities

Lead planning and execution of complex semiconductor and advanced technology facility projects from pre-design through construction administration, ensuring alignment with client objectives, technical requirements, and project delivery milestones.
Develop and manage project scope, budgets, schedules, staffing plans, and execution strategies for large, multidisciplinary design and construction efforts, including design-build and integrated project delivery environments.
Coordinate with discipline leads in mechanical, electrical, plumbing, structural, process, controls, and architectural teams to integrate cleanroom, fab support, utility, and high-performance building systems into cohesive project deliverables.
Guide basis of design development, design narratives, engineering calculations, and technical reviews for facility systems and mission-critical infrastructure.
Oversee QA/QC review gates, interdisciplinary coordination, and milestone deliverable reviews to ensure accuracy, constructability, code compliance, and alignment with client standards and operational requirements.
Manage client communication and decision-making throughout the project lifecycle, including executive reporting, design reviews, issue resolution, and presentation of technical impacts.
Direct change management processes, including scope evaluation, budget and schedule impact analysis, contingency planning, and negotiation of modifications with clients, contractors, and internal teams.
Coordinate with vendors, equipment suppliers, and specialty consultants to support equipment integration, procurement planning, utility interfaces, and technical submittal review for critical systems and long-lead items.
Lead construction administration activities such as RFIs, submittals, field observations, site walks, punch list coordination, and resolution of design or installation issues during construction and turnover.
Identify project risks early and implement mitigation strategies related to design complexity, schedule constraints, phased occupancy, safety, permitting, and operational continuity.
Promote a strong safety culture by coordinating with project teams and contractors to address life safety, construction safety, and operational risk considerations throughout project delivery.
Mentor project team members and emerging project managers, reinforcing best practices in communication, technical coordination, documentation control, and client service.
Contribute to pursuit support, proposal development, and project planning efforts for new semiconductor and advanced technology opportunities as needed.

Demonstrated project management experience of 10 or more years, with significant focus on the design and delivery of industrial, advanced technology, or high-tech manufacturing facilities such as semiconductor fabrication facilities, data centers, or similar mission-critical environments.
Proven experience leading projects in a design-build or integrated project delivery environment, with responsibility for scope, schedule, budget, quality, and client satisfaction.

Experience coordinating multidisciplinary teams and managing complex interfaces among owners, architects, engineers, contractors, vendors, and commissioning partners.
Working knowledge of project controls, change management, risk management, QA/QC processes, and construction administration practices.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to lead meetings, present technical information clearly, and build trusted client relationships.
